title: Groundbreak 2026: Putting the future of construction to work
summary: From unveiling more than 50 new capabilities to celebrating $2 million in donations and pledges for construction mental health, Groundbreak 2026 showcased the innovation, people, and partnerships shaping the future of construction.
body_markdown:
> *“Procore was founded for you. We are focused solely on the built world. On you. That’s all we do. After all, you are building the places where we live. Where we work. Where we heal.”*
>
>
> *– Ajei Gopal, president and CEO of Procore*


What a week it’s been!


At Groundbreak 2026, we shared our vision for Procore’s evolution into a system of intelligence for the built world, helping construction teams see what’s happening on a jobsite, understand it in context, and act with confidence.


We also announced more than 50 new capabilities designed to bring that vision to life, connecting every stage of the construction lifecycle, from planning and building to operations. **It’s what this year’s theme–Built on Intelligence–is all about: strengthening the core tools customers rely on every day, from submittals, scheduling, and procurement to collaboration across teams, while advancing AI that helps them work smarter.**


That’s on top of new and expanded partnerships designed to help the industry better connect people, data, and technology across the entire construction lifecycle.


But perhaps most importantly, we continued growing our community. Groundbreak 2026 was our **largest gathering yet** , bringing together a record-breaking 5,000+ construction professionals in person and thousands more virtually to share ideas, address industry challenges, learn from one another, and explore what comes next.


It’s been fantastic to see what people have already done with all of these new innovations, and there’s so much more to explore. Here’s a look at where we’re heading.


(Photo by: Carli Beth Photography)


### Strengthening the tools owners and contractors rely on


Owners across the industry are facing the same challenge: their portfolios are growing, but their teams and resources are not. They have to decide where capital goes, balance competing priorities, and identify risks earlier. This requires consistency in how they collect information, make decisions, and learn from what happened during construction.


**Capital Management** (launching next month) works to address these challenges and closes a major gap for owners of hospitals, data centers, manufacturing facilities, and other complex projects. It gives them a portfolio-level view of their capital investments, what they’re planning, what they’ve committed, what they’re forecasting, and where they’re at risk. All while connecting that back to what's actually happening in the field.


Together with[Concept Projects, Owners Hub, Portfolio Monitoring](https://www.procore.com/press/procore-introduces-new-suite-of-portfolio-management-and-capital-planning-capabilities-for-owners-powered-by-procore-ai) , and[Asset Management](https://www.procore.com/press/procore-introduces-asset-register-within-asset-management-to-simplify-handover-from-contractor-to-owner) , we're continuing the momentum of a year-long development journey to help owners plan across their portfolios, understand how their investments are funded, and stay connected with what's happening in real-time. The impact of that visibility is real, with the Dodge Construction Network 2025 ROI report noting that[95 percent of owners say having that data at their fingertips increases their confidence in decision-making](https://www.procore.com/ebooks/dodge-roi-report) .


We're also addressing some of the everyday challenges customers have asked us to solve. New scheduling links to submittals and procurement, currently in closed beta, help teams identify how delayed approvals or material deliveries could affect work on site. And with Procore Connect for RFIs entering open beta, general contractors and specialty contractors can collaborate from their own Procore accounts, reducing duplicate data entry and back-and-forth emails.


Before work starts, daily hazard assessments and toolbox talks help crews plan around the risks in the day’s tasks, while **Safety Hub** gives safety leaders a view of where risk is building across projects.


Once work is underway, Procore AI helps teams prepare and review submittals and flag what doesn’t match the spec. **Procurement Log** , currently in closed beta, connects material deliveries to the project schedule, and AI-assisted timesheet capture helps cut down on manual entry. For leaders, **Insights and Portfolio Hub** show where costs are trending and where work is getting held up.


Because these tools draw on the same project data, the field records can inform what the office decides.


These tools serve different phases of construction, but they’re better together. By connecting the workflows and information teams rely on every day, we’re helping them spend less time piecing together information, and more time moving projects forward.


That’s Built on Intelligence in action: strengthening the core platform customers depend on while laying the foundation for AI that can turn connected project information into meaningful insights and action.


### **AI that understands construction**


The construction industry faces a growing workforce challenge. According to Associated Builders and Contractors,[the U.S. industry will need to attract nearly half a million new workers in 2027 to meet demand](https://www.abc.org/News-Media/News-Releases/abc-construction-industry-must-attract-349000-workers-in-2026-despite-macroeconomic-headwinds) . With teams already stretched thin, making the most of their time has never been more important.


On a construction site, one simple question can send a team searching through drawings, specifications, and project documents. AI makes finding those answers much easier. But putting AI to work in the field isn’t just about faster insights. It’s about helping teams do more with the resources they have, giving them trusted answers right where the work happens.


[Procore AI Go](https://www.procore.com/press/procore-launches-voice-first-ai-mobile-app-built-for-the-jobsite) , a new voice-first mobile app entering open beta, lets construction professionals ask questions out loud even on noisy construction sites and get answers grounded in their project information, right from their phones.


To extend the voice experience, **Procore is also partnering with Meta to bring Procore AI Go to AI glasses** , giving construction crews a hands-free way to access project information and capture first-person photos by simply saying “Hey Procore,” without stopping work to reach for a phone.


Delivering useful answers starts with AI that truly understands construction. According to research from FMI,[90% of data generated in engineering and construction is unstructured](https://fmicorp.com/uploads/media/FMI_BigDataReport.pdf) . That means valuable project information is often scattered across drawings, documents, photos, and other formats. Unlocking its potential requires more than simply finding information. It requires understanding the intricate relationships across everything that happens on a project, spanning teams, systems, and workflows.


That’s what makes **Magpie 3.0** , the latest model powering Procore AI’s reasoning engine, so exciting. Now in open beta, Magpie 3.0 builds on **more than 20 years of Procore’s construction expertise** , combining deep, construction-specific intelligence with our multimodal index to connect information across drawings, RFIs, plans, photos, and more. By making sense of these complex relationships, it can uncover insights that general-purpose AI models might miss.


The results speak for themselves. In testing across more than 200 real-world construction tasks, independently reviewed by a lecturer at Cal Poly San Luis Obispo’s School of Construction Education, **Magpie 3.0 outperformed the strongest general-purpose AI model tested by 18 percentage points.**


And now we’re making it easier for customers to access the expertise that only Procore AI can deliver in the other tools they use.


With **Procore AI MCP** , companies will be able to securely connect their enterprise Claude environment to Procore AI, with support for additional AI providers coming in 2027. This brings Procore AI’s deep understanding of construction projects directly into the AI tools customers already use.


Imagine asking Claude to help prepare for your next project meeting or generate a detailed status report. Behind the scenes, Claude calls on Procore AI to find the right project records, apply user permissions, and reason through the information. Procore AI then returns relevant information with references to the source data, allowing Claude to create a report grounded in what’s actually happening on the job.


> *“The request starts in Claude. The construction intelligence comes from Procore AI.”*
>
>
> *– Thiago da Costa, SVP of AI & Data at Procore*


The new[Procore Agent Marketplace](https://marketplace.procore.com/) expands what’s possible even further, bringing specialized AI agents from trusted partners into Procore. Agents can also help with time-consuming tasks, like turning jobsite notes and photos into daily reports or checking documents for missing information.


Together, these announcements represent a shift from AI that simply finds information to AI that understands construction, connects expertise across the industry and acts alongside people to get work done.


### **The power of partnerships for improving project views, from start to finish**


Procore expanded its[collaboration](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/european-ecosystem-builds-worlds-most-efficient-ai-factories-with-nvidia-dsx) with NVIDIA,[adding another dimension](https://www.procore.com/press/procore-collaborates-with-nvidia-to-deliver-advanced-digital-twin-capabilities-to-predict-and-minimize-risks-for-megaprojects) . Currently in closed beta, teams can now move seamlessly between Procore’s Model Manager and Realism Mode, powered by[NVIDIA Omniverse libraries](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/omniverse/) , to visualize projects in a physically accurate 3D environment. By simulating real-world conditions such as extreme weather *before* they happen on the jobsite, teams can make adjustments that avoid costly rework, delays, and schedule disruption.


We announced a[collaboration with IBM](https://www.procore.com/press/procore-announces-collaboration-with-ibm-focused-on-enhancing-asset-lifecycle-management-for-capital-project-owners-and-operators) focused on connecting Procore Asset Management with[IBM Maximo Application Suite](https://www.ibm.com/products/maximo) to help bring construction asset information into the systems used to maintain buildings and equipment after they open. Most construction project owners have spent more time than they’d care to admit trying to gather accurate project data from disconnected systems and teams. This collaboration aims to enable a connected digital thread of critical data across the fixed asset lifecycle, helping optimize the handover process and accelerate operational readiness.


Additionally, we’ve streamlined construction context, governance, and model infrastructure by partnering with AWS, integrating Procore and **Amazon Bedrock** . New generative AI models and multimodal capabilities are arriving at high speeds. This collaboration guarantees your jobsite technology will be among the cutting-edge, all while keeping your data secure.


We’re also delighted to share new capabilities from **DroneDeploy** , the leader in reality capture and visual intelligence, which Procore[acquired earlier this year](https://www.procore.com/blog/procore-acquires-dronedeploy-to-bring-visual-intelligence-to-every-jobsite) . Mobile 3D scanning can document spaces that may wind up behind walls or underground, such as pipes, electrical systems, and structural components, before they’re closed off. Visual AI analyzes site images to check construction progress and clarify potential safety hazards. Connecting reality capture with project models and records can illuminate discrepancies, such as a piece of equipment being installed in a different location than originally planned.


Together, these capabilities bring construction teams closer to the work, enabling them to **see** the job from virtually any angle, **understand** what’s happening through AI-driven reasoning and construction expertise, and **act** on issues before they become costly problems. The result is a clearer picture of what’s happening across every project and the insights needed to keep work moving forward.

### **Beyond the technology: Conversations at Groundbreak 2026**


> “There’s something really special about being surrounded by people who are genuinely excited about the future of construction. Groundbreak brings together some of the brightest minds in the industry, and you leave inspired by the innovation happening today and what’s possible next.”
>
>
> – Jackie Fisher, VP of People + Culture Juneau Construction Company & 2026 Groundbreaker Award Winner in the Category of ‘Building for Tomorrow’


Each year, Groundbreak is an opportunity for us to share our latest product and company news, though this event has always been more than just what we announce. What makes Groundbreak so special is that it connects the people who understand construction’s challenges firsthand and provides opportunities to learn from one another and share their own experiences. We saw those connections happening all week long.


One of the floor’s most energetic areas was the **Procore AI Zone** , a hands-on proving ground where attendees didn’t just hear about the future of AI; they experienced it alongside the engineers building the technology. From streamlining everyday workflows to tackling time-consuming administrative tasks, attendees got a firsthand look at how AI can help solve some of construction’s most persistent challenges.


Attendees got a high-level look at our growing suite of pre-built agents designed to tackle everyday workflows, as well as custom Agent Studio workflows to tailor agents that fit specific operational needs. This intelligence extends even further through the **Agent Marketplace** , which allows teams to deploy specialized partner agents directly into their Procore environment. Backing all of this is the new **Control Tower** , giving admins full transparency over AI usage to ensure predictable scaling.


The **Innovation Lab** brought the power of Procore closer to where work happens: the jobsite. Attendees test-drove **Procore AI Go** , our new voice-first mobile AI experience, and **Meta AI Glasses** , exploring how technology can put critical project information at their fingertips. The goal? Give contractors the insights and answers they need to keep work moving, without heading back to the trailer or digging through documents.


[Procore Launches Voice-First AI Mobile App Built for the Jobsite](https://www.procore.com/press/procore-launches-voice-first-ai-mobile-app-built-for-the-jobsite)

[AI That Understands the Job, Not Just the Document](https://www.procore.com/blog/ai-that-understands-the-job-not-just-the-document)


Those conversations carried on at **Ground Brew** . Industry professionals met to exchange ideas, share challenges, and discover opportunities that are shaping their work. Our small-group, peer-learning sessions, facilitated by Braindates, were a hit, drawing almost 500 attendees across 80+ peer-led sessions. These discussions gave attendees an opportunity to learn from one another, share practical insights, and explore new ways to drive success long after Groundbreak.


### **A community-driven pledge for mental health**


We announced plenty of exciting updates at Groundbreak 2026, yet some of the most meaningful progress went beyond technology. At Procore, our vision is to improve the lives of everyone in construction. That means not only transforming how the industry works, but also supporting the people who make it possible.


Since 2023, Procore and The B1M have worked together to bring greater awareness to mental health in construction through the[Get Construction Talking Pledge](https://www.getconstructiontalking.org/) . With the support of the industry, we’ve surpassed $1 million raised for charities providing critical mental health resources and support. And at Groundbreak 2026, we announced an anonymous donor’s commitment of an additional $1 million over the next decade, bringing the total raised and pledged to more than $2 million.


Technology empowers us to do more, but construction remains an industry built by people. Their mental health is just as critical as the physical tools they use. To ensure our workforce gets the support they need, all funds raised go directly toward funding mental health resources, suicide prevention, and crisis care for construction workers.


This money directly finances five dedicated charity partners across the globe: CIASP, Lighthouse, Construction Sport, Mates in Mind, and Mates in Construction. Spanning the US, UK, Ireland, Australia, and New Zealand, this effort reflects what’s possible when the industry unites to protect the minds that build our world.


> "It’s completely surreal. In 2023, raising $1 million felt like a crazy dream. Hitting that mark—and then being floored by an anonymous match that will make it $2 million in the coming years—is a testament to this industry. I’m incredibly grateful to our donors, the construction community, our charity partners, The B1M, and Procore. But the true milestone goes far beyond the money. It’s about breaking the silence on the jobsite, getting people the help they need, and saving lives."
>
>
> – Fred Mills, founder of The B1M


### **Building what’s next, together**


Launching over 50 new capabilities is a massive step forward, yet Groundbreak 2026 was about more than the technology.


These tools prove that when construction becomes simpler and smarter, builders get back the time and power to do what they do best: build amazing things. **That's the promise of Built on Intelligence. We’re continuing to improve the tools customers depend on today while unlocking new possibilities for how the industry works tomorrow.**


Groundbreak 2026 is officially a wrap, but what we’re building together is just getting started. Join us in Anaheim, California, for Groundbreak 2027 as we continue shaping the future of construction together.
